name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Adversaries obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain access, maintain persistence, or escalate privileges.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or hash values are obtained.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, often via encoded or obfuscated commands.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: Adversaries communicate using application layer protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) to blend in with normal traffic, often for C2.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including scanning for vulnerabilities.

name: Active Scanning
description: Adversaries actively probe target infrastructure for exploitable weaknesses prior to compromise.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries use valid accounts to log into remote services for lateral movement across a network.

name: Masquerading
description: Adversaries manipulate features of artifacts to make them appear legitimate or benign.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries inject code into processes to evade defenses and elevate privileges.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries encode or obfuscate content to make it harder to discover or analyze.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Adversaries abuse task scheduling functionality to execute code or maintain persistence.

name: Create or Modify System Process
description: Adversaries create or modify system-level processes (e.g. services) to maintain persistence.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevation of privileges.

name: Impair Defenses
description: Adversaries disable or modify security tools to avoid detection.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries dump credentials from the operating system to obtain account information.

name: Unsecured Credentials
description: Adversaries search for credentials stored in insecure locations such as files or configs.

name: Account Discovery
description: Adversaries attempt to get a listing of accounts on a system or within an environment.

name: Remote System Discovery
description: Adversaries attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Adversaries attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware.

name: Process Discovery
description: Adversaries attempt to get information about running processes on a system.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment.

name: Proxy
description: Adversaries use a connection proxy to direct network traffic and disguise the source/destination of C2 traffic.

name: Encrypted Channel
description: Adversaries employ encryption to conceal command and control traffic.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries encrypt data to interrupt availability, e.g. ransomware.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Adversaries delete or disable system recovery features to prevent restoration.

name: Account Access Removal
description: Adversaries interrupt availability by deleting or locking accounts used by legitimate users.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit a weakness in an internet-facing host or system to gain initial access.

name: External Remote Services
description: Adversaries leverage external remote services (VPN, RDP, Citrix) to gain initial access or persist.

name: Email Collection
description: Adversaries target user email to collect sensitive information.

name: Screen Capture
description: Adversaries capture screen images to gather sensitive information visible to a user.

name: Service Stop
description: Adversaries stop or disable services to render systems unavailable.

name: Remote Access Software
description: Adversaries use legitimate desktop support and remote access software as a C2 channel.
